tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.

tools.name: js
tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

If the user specifies an app to use, get the app by name, bundle ID, or path:

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp("Example App");
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Each `cua_repl.js` call opens or continues a browser activity. Keep consecutive calls together. The activity stays open across messages until you emit completion commentary.

**Manual takeover takes priority over the table below.** For a required manual browser step, call the documented takeover API before asking the user to act, unless takeover is already pending. Explain the required step in your final reply. Tab marking alone does not transfer control. While waiting for the user to finish and return control, emit no completion and make no CUA calls, even when answering side questions. The takeover API returning does not end this wait. When the user returns or unblocks you, resume browser work and apply the table. If they cancel, replace, or no longer need the browser work, close the activity before answering, even without another CUA call.

Completion is a standalone assistant commentary message containing only `::browser-complete{title="<headline>"}`. Never put it in a tool call or final reply. Use 3–6 words starting with a past-tense verb to describe the observed outcome. Omit identifiers.

After a user cancels pending browser work: commentary `::browser-complete{title="Stopped browser work"}`, then the final acknowledgement. No browser call is needed.

For an open browser activity:

| Next action                                   | Required output order                                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Another CUA call                              | Continue without completion.                                                              |
| A non-CUA tool, final reply, or chat question | Finish required tab marking, emit completion, then take that action in the same response. |

With no open activity, emit no completion. Later CUA use requires a fresh completion at the next table boundary.

If you need a one-time sign-in code, information, or confirmation from the user, follow the table and ask in chat. One-time code entry alone does not require takeover. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

tools.name: js_reset
tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

Spawn one `goldfish-explorer` per chunk in parallel, at most 5 at a time (queue the rest), give each chunk the file's imports and top-level definitions to judge visibility, and merge their JSON. Verify build-manifest deps and `import` / `#include` before attributing RPCs, schemas, or message types locally. Read order: (1) contracts, schemas, build manifests (`.h`, `.hh`, `.hpp`, `.proto`, `.graphql`, `.gql`, `.thrift`, `.prisma`, `.sql` DDL, interfaces; extract exact DDL tables and exported targets); (2) entry points (`main.*`, `index.*`, `lib.*`, `mod.*`, `__init__.py`, dir-named files) then source/query files alphabetically; (3) templates/configs <= 200 lines each (800 in config-only dirs), excluding `.css`/`.scss`; (4) ignore test files (`*_test.*`, `*Test.*`, `test_*.*`, `*.spec.*`) everywhere. On scout timeout/failure, log a warning and use `["(Details pending/documentation failed)"]`.
    *   **Parent Propagation**: Pass merged child `interface` summaries into parent `P`'s scout prompt.
    *   **Verification Commands**: Use `VerificationCommand` or the manifest in `D` or nearest ancestor (.NET: `dotnet test` on the nearest `*.csproj`). For Bazel, always emit `bazel test` or `bazel build` with valid targets (`//[package_path]/...` or `//[package_path]:all`; NEVER `//[package_path]...`, `//[package_path]:...`, or bare `...`); use `bazel run` for runners.
    *   **Template & Link Policy**: Read [README templates](references/templates.md) before writing. Use **Component Package (Peanuts)** when `D` has direct code (plus child contract links if any) and **Intermediate Blueprint** when `D` has only child contracts. Use relative links (`./child/${target_filename}`, `../sibling/${target_filename}`) **only** for dirs existing in pruned `subtree_index` with real files (link `./child/SKILL.md` for skill dirs or omit uncreated links), and repo/URL links for external cross-package refs. Format cleanly.
3.  **Report or Continue**: Compile `subtree_index` (`path`, `summary`, `interface`, `invariants`, `side_effects`). If `is_worker` is `true`, read [Worker Return Interface Schema](references/worker-return.schema.json), return the matching JSON payload, and stop. Otherwise proceed to **Step 5**.

### Step 5: Root Compilation & Termination (Root Orchestrator)

1.  **Collect Worker Payloads**: Merge `subtree_index` JSON results. On worker timeout/failure, insert `[Subtree Root] (Documentation failed / Subagent execution timeout)` in the root index and continue.
2.  **Intermediate Directories**: Read [README templates](references/templates.md) if not already loaded, and document intermediate folders between `path` and partition roots bottom-up using the **Intermediate Blueprint** template and valid relative links.
3.  **Root Contract (`path`)**: Always classify `path` as **Repository Root (Blueprint / Hay)** using the **Repository Root Blueprint Template**, rolling up all top-level subdirectory boundaries. Preserve existing top title/metadata/overview via Correction Policy if `target_filename` exists. If `path` has direct source files, scout them via `goldfish-explorer` into `## Local Interface & Invariants`. Ensure root diagrams reflect only verified sync/async boundaries, operations, and stores from `subtree_index`, then write `target_filename`.
4.  **Final Correctness Verification (CRITICAL)**: Re-read **every** created or modified contract file in `subtree_index` (including all child packages) and verify:
    *   `Interface`, `Invariants`, and `Side Effects` sections cite verified `[file:symbol_or_flag]` entries (or `None`) without unverified claims.
    *   Valid Markdown headers, tables, fences, and Bazel/test targets (`/...` or `:all`, never `:...`).
    *   Every relative link (`./subdir/${target_filename}`, `./subdir/SKILL.md`) points to an existing file on disk (remove or fix broken links).
5.  **Optional Drift Review**: Present a single-select gate (`is_multi_select: false`):
    *   `question`: `"Do you want to run the EGM Drift Report on the generated contract updates to check for consistency with the codebase?"`
    *   `options`: `["(Recommended) Yes, run drift report on modified contracts", "No, skip drift review"]`
    If selected, run [egm-drift-report](../egm-drift-report/SKILL.md) over modified contracts to check both missing code coverage and doc-to-code hallucinations (verifying every documented method, route, enum, database table, and invariant against local source files and recording discrepancies in the drift report for human triage).
6.  Terminate cleanly.

*   **ONE QUESTION AT A TIME (CRITICAL)**: You are strictly forbidden from
    asking more than one question in a single response. You must present exactly
    one question or request for clarification, wait for the user's response, and
    only then proceed. Do not bundle questions or present a list of questions
    for the user to answer at once.
*   **NO SUMMARIES (CRITICAL)**: You MUST NOT include a "Summary of work",

*   **Contradiction Auditing (MUST ENFORCE - CRITICAL)**: If you detect a

# Harnesses

EGM is one set of skills and personas. This repository serves as the
plugin source for each supported harness. No harness gets a fork of the skill
text.

| Antigravity CLI | `agy plugin install https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model` |
| Antigravity App | Run `/plugin` or see [installation instructions](#antigravity-app-and-antigravity-for-ides) |
| Antigravity for IDEs | Run `/plugin` or see [installation instructions](#antigravity-app-and-antigravity-for-ides) |
| Antigravity IDE (standalone) | Not supported; see [installation instructions](#antigravity-app-and-antigravity-for-ides) |

break EGM, because the skills read `agents/` and
`resources/document_standards/` at run time.

### Antigravity App and Antigravity for IDEs

- **Antigravity App**: Run `/plugin`, ask the agent `Install https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model`, or manually install into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/` using the commands below.
- **Antigravity for IDEs (Extension for Visual Studio Code)**: Run `/plugin`, ask the agent `Install https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model`, or manually install into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/` using the commands below.
- **Antigravity IDE (Standalone)**: Not supported at this time. Although the plugin and skills load from `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/`, standalone Antigravity IDE (tested on macOS and Linux) does not expose the fresh-context subagent tool (`invoke_subagent`) required for Goldfish reviews (`/egm-brainstorm` and `/egm-review`).

The Antigravity App and Antigravity for IDEs share the global plugin directory
`~/.gemini/config/plugins/<name>/`. For a fresh manual installation without the
`agy` CLI, copy the full runtime bundle into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/`
(copying into an existing plugin directory can leave obsolete files behind, so
remove `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm` first when updating):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model.git
cd elephant-goldfish-model
mkdir -p ~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm
cp -R plugin.json README.md LICENSE skills agents resources docs assets ~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/
```

Reload the window (or restart the Antigravity App), then confirm that `egm`
appears in the plugin list and that its skills (`egm-brainstorm`, `egm-draft`,
`egm-review`) are available. The command form for these skills in the
Antigravity App and Antigravity for IDEs has not been verified.

## Manifests

Root `plugin.json` is the canonical source for plugin identity, version,
description, and publisher metadata. It follows the portable Agent Plugins
1.0.0 format; the `$schema` key is omitted because omp routes manifests that
declare it to a strict validator that rejects `disable-model-invocation`.
Update shared values there first, then update the compatibility
manifests; unit tests reject metadata drift. Keep platform-specific fields in
their existing manifests until installation tests justify removing them.

Marketplace files are discovery catalogs pointing to this package, not copies
of its skills. In particular, `.agents/plugins/` contains the Codex catalog,
while `agents/` contains reviewer personas. All hosts share the same `skills/`,
`agents/`, and `resources/` content.

| Harness | Manifest | Skills | Subagents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Antigravity | `plugin.json` | `skills/` (default) | `agents/` (default) |
| Claude Code | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | `skills/` (default) | Claude adapters and orchestrators listed in `plugin.json` `agents` |
| Claude Cowork | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | `skills/` (default) | Subagents run inside Cowork; hooks n/a |
| Codex | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` | `skills` path | Not shipped; general-purpose subagent reads the persona file |
| ChatGPT | `plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`; `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` for workspace import | `skills` path | Detect native tools in the current session; general-purpose agent reads the persona |
| omp | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (Claude-compatible fallback) | `skills/` (default) | Personas from `agents/`/`.claude-plugin/agents/` register as native `task` agents |
| Muse | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (Claude-compatible fallback) | `skills/` (default) | 10 adapters import as agents; tool projections unsupported |

Persona prompts live in `agents/`, the directory Antigravity
scans for subagents. Each persona has `name` and `description` frontmatter, so
harnesses that load `agents/*.md` register them as named subagents
(`egm-design`, `egm-zoom-out`, and so on).

When you add a reviewer persona, add a Claude adapter under
`.claude-plugin/agents/` and list it in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.
The adapter reads the shared persona and sets Claude's read-only tools and
context isolation. This avoids imposing Claude tool names on other hosts.
In Claude Code, `/plugin` > Errors will report that the default `agents/` folder is ignored because the manifest sets `"agents"`; this warning is expected and harmless (see [Claude integration](claude.md#claude-code-warning-default-agents-folder-is-ignored)).

## Delegation

Skills say "spawn a subagent" and name a persona. Each harness maps that
phrase to its own tool:

| Harness | Subagent tool | Named personas | Nesting |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Antigravity | `invoke_subagent` | Yes | Yes |
| Claude Code | Agent (Task) tool | Yes | Up to 3 levels by default |
| Claude Cowork | Cowork subagents | Yes | Subagents run inside Cowork |
| Codex | Native spawn/wait tools; inspect the available schema | No | Detect at runtime; direct dispatch fallback |
| ChatGPT | Native spawn/wait tools when exposed by the current Work session | No | Detect at runtime; direct dispatch fallback |
| omp | `task` tool | Yes | Yes |
| Muse | Native subagents; inspect the available schema | Named spawn rejected in 1.4.14; general-purpose fallback verified | Detect at runtime; direct dispatch fallback |

Where a harness has no named persona, the skill spawns a general-purpose
subagent and tells it to read `agents/<file>.md` first. If a harness cannot
nest subagents, use direct dispatch instead of the synthesizer.

A Goldfish review needs a fresh context. If a harness has no subagent tool,
the review skills stop instead of running in the same context. Check actual
tool availability rather than inferring it from the product name. This applies
to standalone Antigravity IDE and to ChatGPT modes that do not expose native
fresh-context delegation.

Fresh conversation context does not mean that the host omits its instruction
files. Codex's `fork_context: false` and `fork_turns: "none"` isolate parent
turns; they do not establish that project or user instructions are excluded.
Keep stable workspace conventions in instruction files. State review
assumptions that the Goldfish must challenge as explicit review criteria.

## Artifact Directory

Skills write briefs, drafts, and reports to the working directory, or to the
harness's artifact directory if it has one. In Claude Code, Claude Cowork,
Codex, and ChatGPT, you can name another folder. Add this line to your prompt,
or to an agent instructions file that your harness loads (`CLAUDE.md` or
`AGENTS.md`, in the project or at user level):

```text
EGM artifact directory: .dev/docs
```

A relative path is relative to the working directory. If a path set in an
instructions file resolves outside the working directory, after following
symbolic links, EGM asks you to confirm it before creating the folder or
writing there. If you decline or no one can confirm, as in a headless run, the
files go to the working directory. The answer isn't saved, so a new session
asks again. A path in your prompt needs no confirmation. Design docs and other
project files do not move. Claude Code reads a project `AGENTS.md` only when
the project has no `CLAUDE.md`.

Commit approved specifications in `docs/designs/` and project rules in
`AGENTS.md`. Teammates and agents then use the same committed files. Add
`.dev/docs` to `.gitignore` only to keep scratch drafts out of git before
approval.

## Support Status & Contributing Other Harnesses

**Antigravity CLI**, **Claude Code**, and **Codex** pass automated installation
and end-to-end workflow fixtures. Reviewer isolation evidence is narrower:
parent-turn isolation and host-instruction exclusion are separate results.

Claude reviewer adapters set `omitClaudeMd: true`; see the
[Claude integration](claude.md#reviewer-isolation). For Codex, issue [#237](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/237)
reports that Codex CLI 0.166.0 supplied project and user `AGENTS.md` files
despite `fork_turns: "none"`. For Antigravity CLI, the same issue reports
project `AGENTS.md` and `GEMINI.md` in reviewer context. These are reported
host-instruction leaks, not evidence that parent conversation turns leaked.
The Codex test and recorded Antigravity run check parent-turn isolation only;
neither verifies instruction-file exclusion. No host-specific exclusion
control is verified here for Codex or Antigravity.

**Claude Cowork** ([#105](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/105)) and **ChatGPT Work** ([#106](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/106)) have working installation paths with open cloud trace verification gaps. The README's prefix guidance covers only Antigravity (agy CLI), Claude Code, and Codex. For ChatGPT workspace imports, the skills are reached through `@egm` (see [ChatGPT](codex.md#chatgpt)); the command form in Claude Cowork is not recorded yet.

**omp** ([#186](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/186)) has a working installation path. Skills are invoked as `/skill:egm-<command>` (omp registers one command per skill; it has no `/egm-*` namespace). Community-verified on omp v18.12.6: all seven skills discover and resolve, and all nine reviewer personas register as subagents. End-to-end workflow fixtures are not yet automated for omp.

In omp, `skill://` reads are confined to each skill's own folder and reject `..` traversal, so plugin-root assets (`resources/`, `agents/`, `docs/`) cannot be read through `skill://` paths ([#455](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/455)). Until a dedicated omp adapter lands under [#186](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/186), resolve the physical plugin root two directories above the skill folder (for example via `realpath skill://<name>` or the physical path printed in the header of `read skill://<name>`) and read plugin-root assets by absolute path.

**Muse** (1.4.14) has a working installation path. `muse plugins validate` reports the plugin valid with all seven skills and all ten agent adapters supported; every agent tool projection is unsupported, so Claude tool allowlists do not restrict Muse reviewers. Install from a local path; `marketplace add` on this repository discovers zero plugins because Muse reads the Codex catalog first. End-to-end workflow fixtures passed on 2026-10-30 (brainstorm, draft, and uninterrupted review with 15 fresh-context reviewers); named `egm/egm-*` agents cannot be spawned in this runtime, so reviewers used the general-purpose fallback reading the installed persona first. See the [Muse guide](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/docs/muse.md). No skill routes a Muse session to that guide yet ([#252](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/252)), so point the session at it.

**Windsurf** (renamed Devin Desktop on 2026-06-02; [#376](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/376)) has experimental workspace routing. The rule and workflow files resolve the shared `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `agents/*.md`, and `resources/document_standards/*.md` files directly. They do not copy skill text. Goldfish reviews stop if fresh-context, read-only subagent delegation is unavailable, and reviewers launch on the host's read-only subagent profile. Devin CLI 3000.12.43 runs on 2026-11-10 passed routing, human pauses, read-only reviewers, and parent-marker isolation with every file write denied, so no workflow ran to a final artifact. Devin Desktop and the Devin CLI run the same agent, Devin Local, which replaced Cascade. The Devin Desktop IDE remains untested. The CLI does not list `.windsurf/workflows/` as slash commands; `/egm-*` requests route through the rule. Denying a permission prompt ends the host's turn without a message; send a follow-up message to continue. See the [design](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/docs/designs/windsurf_support.md#recorded-cli-evidence-2026-11-10) for the evidence.

See the [harness test record](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/TESTING.md#harness-test-record) for tested surfaces and limits.

We welcome contributors who want to help verify and expand harness support.

### Contributing Support for New Harnesses

A harness counts as supported after `/egm-brainstorm`, `/egm-draft`, and
`/egm-review` run end to end through its plugin install. When contributing
support for another harness:

1. Add the appropriate manifest or configuration file to the repository root

2. Document install steps, manifest mapping, and delegation mechanics in this guide

3. Verify that `/egm-brainstorm`, `/egm-draft`, and `/egm-review` run end to end,

# Codex integration

## Install and locate the plugin

For the desktop app, install the [published EGM plugin](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6aeb90f47ec88191a3c107e01d3eb357). This listing is desktop-only.

For Codex CLI, install the whole plugin, including its personas and standards:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model
codex plugin add egm@egm
```

Start a fresh session after installation. Select the installed `egm` skill
from the available skills. Use its discovered absolute `SKILL.md` path;
do not assume a particular cache directory, version, or checkout location.

From `<plugin>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`, the plugin root is three parent
directories above the file. Resolve bundled `agents/`, `resources/`, and
`docs/` paths against that root. Resolve `references/` against the active
skill's directory. Resolve user documents and generated artifacts against
the user's working directory. Never substitute similarly named files in the
user's project for bundled personas or standards.

If the user's prompt or agent instructions file (`AGENTS.md`) has a line
`EGM artifact directory: <path>`, write briefs, drafts, and reports to that
folder. Resolve a relative path against the working directory. If a path from
`AGENTS.md` resolves outside the working directory, after following symbolic
links, ask the user to confirm it before creating the folder or writing there.
If they decline or no one can confirm, use the working directory and say why.
Create the folder if it does not exist.

In ChatGPT Work, a skill may be exposed through a cloud resource identifier
while supporting files live in the installed local bundle. Use the installed
path supplied by the skill inventory or installation metadata for those files;
do not construct cloud resource identifiers for arbitrary supporting paths.
If no installed path is available, report the missing capability instead of
guessing a cache location. Read reviewer filenames and frontmatter from the
bundle: a role such as `egm-design` maps to `agents/design_critic.md`, not
`agents/design.md`. Confirm each resolved path before dispatch.

## Fresh-context reviewers

Inspect the available native subagent tool schema. Tool names can be
namespaced and vary by Codex version. When `spawn_agent` exposes
`fork_context`, explicitly set `fork_context: false` for every Goldfish.
When the schema instead exposes `fork_turns`, use `fork_turns: "none"`.
This applies to reviewers launched by a synthesizer too. Use a general-purpose agent
and pass absolute paths to the persona, standards, target document, and
explicitly selected reading list. Do not pass the parent transcript, private
reasoning, or answers the document is supposed to explain.

Require the reviewer to read its persona, target, and every supplied standard
before returning findings. A missing read or inaccessible file is an incomplete
review, not a clean result. Verify native tool results when the host exposes
them; a parent-written completion summary is not equivalent evidence.

Wait for actual reviewer completion before synthesizing findings. Propagate
failures and timeouts; a launched reviewer is not a completed review. If
nesting is unavailable, dispatch reviewers directly from the parent while
preserving the same isolation. If the available tool cannot establish a fresh
context, stop the Goldfish review and report that limitation.

Fresh conversation context does not isolate the filesystem, configured memory
services, or project instructions. Do not retrieve conversation history or
memory to supply missing design context. An isolation test should use a unique
parent-only marker and check the actual child result, not the parent's claim.

The `fork_context: false` and `fork_turns: "none"` options concern parent
conversation turns. They do not prove that Codex excludes host instruction
files. Issue [#237](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/237)
reports that Codex CLI 0.166.0 injected project and user `AGENTS.md` files
despite `fork_turns: "none"`. Treat instruction-file exclusion as unverified
unless a separate child-context probe confirms it for the tested host version.

## Questions and artifacts

The shared skills' question payloads describe the intended interaction, not a
literal Codex API. Use a structured question tool only when it is available
and permitted in the current mode, mapping to its actual schema. Otherwise
ask one plain-text question and wait for the answer. Preserve the skill's
readiness and section approval gates; tool unavailability is not approval.

Link generated artifacts with absolute-path Markdown links such as
`[design draft](/absolute/project/design_draft.md)`. For paths containing
spaces use `[design draft](</absolute/my project/design_draft.md>)`.
Do not use `file://` links in Codex chat.

## Verification

Run the offline packaging checks with `pytest tests/unit`. The opt-in native
workflow tests are documented in [TESTING.md](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/TESTING.md). They require
an authenticated Codex CLI and consume model usage. Installing or discovering
the plugin alone does not establish end-to-end workflow support.

## ChatGPT

Install the [published EGM plugin](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6aeb90f47ec88191a3c107e01d3eb357) in the ChatGPT desktop app. This listing is desktop-only; it does not establish support for cloud Work sessions.

# Execution Instructions

This file holds bundled execution rules shared across multiple Elephant-Goldfish
Model (EGM) skills, plus drafting-only rules used strictly by `egm-draft`. Only
apply the sections referenced by the active skill.

## Plugin-Root Resource Paths

Bundled personas (`agents/<file>.md`), standards
(`resources/document_standards/<name>.md`), harness guides (`docs/*.md`), and
this file (`resources/execution_instructions.md`) sit at the plugin root, two
directories above each skill's folder (`<plugin-root>/skills/<skill-name>/`).

*   **Local / relative path**: Read `../../resources/execution_instructions.md`
    (or `<plugin-root>/<path>`).
*   **Claude Code and Cowork**: Read
    `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/resources/execution_instructions.md` (or
    `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path>`).
*   **Pathless `<SKILL>` injection**: If the harness injects a skill without its
    file path, check `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/<path>`.

Pass spawned subagents the resolved absolute paths of their persona file and
standard when `<plugin-root>` is known. A failed skill-relative lookup does not
mean the file is absent from the plugin.
Never substitute workspace files with similar names for bundled personas,
standards, or execution instructions. If you cannot read a required plugin-root
file after resolving `<plugin-root>`, say so instead of calling it missing; apply
the active skill's inline fallback only when file tools are unavailable.

## Subagent Delegation (Goldfish Isolation)

Applies to subagent-spawning skills (`egm-bootstrap`, `egm-brainstorm`,
`egm-review`, and `egm-review-loop`):

A Goldfish runs in a fresh context with no conversation history. Spawn each
subagent with your harness's subagent tool (Antigravity: `invoke_subagent`;
Claude Code: `Agent`; Codex: `spawn_agent`). Each subagent is defined in
`agents/<file>.md`, and its frontmatter `name` (for example `egm-zoom-out`) is
the subagent type to request where your harness registers named subagents.
Otherwise spawn a general-purpose subagent and tell it to read that persona
file first. Pass prompts verbatim and wait for the report. If your harness
cannot nest subagents, use direct dispatch instead of `egm-synthesizer` (see
[harnesses.md](../docs/harnesses.md)). If your harness has no subagent tool,
follow the active skill's fallback rule (`egm-bootstrap` runs scout steps
inline; `egm-review`, `egm-brainstorm`, and `egm-review-loop` stop and tell the
user that a review in the same context is not a Goldfish review).

## Shared Design & Review Constraints

Applies strictly to `egm-brainstorm`, `egm-draft`, and `egm-review` (not
`egm-bootstrap`):

*   **Artifact-First Delivery (MANDATORY)**: You are **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN** from
    presenting large proposals, drafts, summaries, or review reports directly in
    the chat pane. Write them directly to the working directory (or your
    harness's artifact directory, if one is configured) via your file-writing
    tool, share the file path or clickable link in chat, and ask the user for
    review.
*   **Plain-English Standard**: Write concepts briefs, specs, summaries,
    reports, and communications in simple, direct, jargon-free plain English.
    Explain technical mechanisms concretely. Do not summarize away substance or
    rely on buzzwords, promotional adjectives (*seamless*, *robust*,
    *blazingly fast*), or decorative adverbs (*seamlessly*, *effortlessly*,
    *literally*, *drastically*, *obviously*).
*   **Adversarial Rigor (No Sycophancy)**: Never agree by default. Stress-test
    ideas, strategies, and opinions to find weak points, edge cases, and blind
    spots before affirming anything. Lead with what is wrong, missing, or risky
    before highlighting merits. Never parrot user framing or validate asserted
    conclusions reflexively; surface what the user is missing, the strongest
    counter-argument, and whether the opposing view holds. Only agree after
    rigorous, objective scrutiny.
    *   **Banned Adjectives (No Flattery)**: Never use validating adjectives
        like `"brilliant"`, `"great"`, `"smart"`, `"correct"`, `"perfect"`,
        `"excellent"`, or `"spot-on"` on the user's inputs, corrections, or
        decisions.
    *   **Banned Apologies**: Never output polite apologies (e.g., `"I
        apologize"`, `"I am sorry"`, `"Forgive me"`) when challenged or
        corrected. State the corrected technical logic and trade-offs directly.
*   **Interaction Invariants**: Every interactive single-select gate (structured
    question tool such as `ask_question`, if your harness has one, or plain
    chat) MUST contain strictly one question (`len(questions) == 1`), set
    `is_multi_select: false`, provide clear action-oriented options without
    `(Recommended)` prefixes, never emit a structured question call with empty
    visible chat text, and be the sole tool call in its model response step
    (finish preparatory file reads or writes in an earlier step of the turn
    first, then output visible chat text and invoke the gate alone to yield).
    Ask open-ended text inputs (such as file paths or lists) in plain chat.

## Drafting-Only Execution Rules (`egm-draft` Only)

Applies **strictly** during `egm-draft` (never during `egm-bootstrap`,
`egm-review`, or other workflows):

*   **Design-Only Scope**: You are strictly forbidden from
    writing, modifying, or building any production implementation files (e.g.,
    `.h`, `.cc`, `.py`, `.go`) in the source tree. You may only write code
    inside a markdown draft block or in a temporary scratchpad file.
    *   **Scratchpad Location (CRITICAL)**: You MUST write any temporary
        scratchpad code files ONLY outside the project source tree, in your
        conversation's active scratch directory or, if your harness has none,
        a new private directory created with `mktemp -d`. If neither is
        available, keep the code in a markdown draft block. Do not use fixed,
        shared paths such as `/tmp/scratch.py`. You are STRICTLY FORBIDDEN
        from creating `.h`, `.cc`, `.py`, `.go`, or any other code files
        anywhere inside the project source tree.
    *   **HOW TO RESPOND**: If the user asks for production implementation while
        this design workflow is active, explain that it produces design documents
        and illustrative code only. Label any markdown or scratchpad example
        clearly. Do not imply that production files were changed. Ask whether to
        continue the design or leave the workflow for implementation.
*   **Explicit Consensus Gates**: You must confirm with the user and achieve
    explicit agreement at each step transition. Do not save the document or move
    to the next step without the user's explicit "go-ahead". Do not move on
    easily. Challenge the user at every step.
*   **ONE QUESTION AT A TIME (CRITICAL)**: You are strictly forbidden from
    asking more than one question in a single response. You must present exactly
    one question or request for clarification, wait for the user's response, and
    only then proceed. Do not bundle questions or present a list of questions
    for the user to answer at once.
*   **NO SUMMARIES (CRITICAL)**: You MUST NOT include a "Summary of work",
    "Status", "Adherence", or "Rule checklist" in your final response. Respond
    only with the technical content and next steps.
*   **Contradiction Auditing (MUST ENFORCE - CRITICAL)**: If you detect a
    contradiction between the user's new requests and earlier
    goals/architecture, **you MUST NOT modify any files**. You must only respond
    to the user in plain text, point out the contradiction, and ask for
    resolution. You are strictly forbidden from planning or executing any
    file-writing/editing tool in the same turn as you discover a contradiction.

## Manifests

Root `plugin.json` is the canonical source for plugin identity, version,
description, and publisher metadata. It follows the portable Agent Plugins
1.0.0 format; the `$schema` key is omitted because omp routes manifests that
declare it to a strict validator that rejects `disable-model-invocation`.
Update shared values there first, then update the compatibility
manifests; unit tests reject metadata drift. Keep platform-specific fields in
their existing manifests until installation tests justify removing them.

Marketplace files are discovery catalogs pointing to this package, not copies
of its skills. In particular, `.agents/plugins/` contains the Codex catalog,
while `agents/` contains reviewer personas. All hosts share the same `skills/`,
`agents/`, and `resources/` content.

| Harness | Manifest | Skills | Subagents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Antigravity | `plugin.json` | `skills/` (default) | `agents/` (default) |
| Claude Code | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | `skills/` (default) | Claude adapters and orchestrators listed in `plugin.json` `agents` |
| Claude Cowork | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | `skills/` (default) | Subagents run inside Cowork; hooks n/a |
| Codex | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` | `skills` path | Not shipped; general-purpose subagent reads the persona file |
| ChatGPT | `plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`; `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` for workspace import | `skills` path | Detect native tools in the current session; general-purpose agent reads the persona |
| omp | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (Claude-compatible fallback) | `skills/` (default) | Personas from `agents/`/`.claude-plugin/agents/` register as native `task` agents |
| Muse | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (Claude-compatible fallback) | `skills/` (default) | 10 adapters import as agents; tool projections unsupported |

Persona prompts live in `agents/`, the directory Antigravity
scans for subagents. Each persona has `name` and `description` frontmatter, so
harnesses that load `agents/*.md` register them as named subagents
(`egm-design`, `egm-zoom-out`, and so on).

When you add a reviewer persona, add a Claude adapter under
`.claude-plugin/agents/` and list it in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.
The adapter reads the shared persona and sets Claude's read-only tools and
context isolation. This avoids imposing Claude tool names on other hosts.
In Claude Code, `/plugin` > Errors will report that the default `agents/` folder is ignored because the manifest sets `"agents"`; this warning is expected and harmless (see [Claude integration](claude.md#claude-code-warning-default-agents-folder-is-ignored)).

## Delegation

Skills say "spawn a subagent" and name a persona. Each harness maps that
phrase to its own tool:

| Harness | Subagent tool | Named personas | Nesting |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Antigravity | `invoke_subagent` | Yes | Yes |
| Claude Code | Agent (Task) tool | Yes | Up to 3 levels by default |
| Claude Cowork | Cowork subagents | Yes | Subagents run inside Cowork |
| Codex | Native spawn/wait tools; inspect the available schema | No | Detect at runtime; direct dispatch fallback |
| ChatGPT | Native spawn/wait tools when exposed by the current Work session | No | Detect at runtime; direct dispatch fallback |
| omp | `task` tool | Yes | Yes |
| Muse | Native subagents; inspect the available schema | Named spawn rejected in 1.4.14; general-purpose fallback verified | Detect at runtime; direct dispatch fallback |

Where a harness has no named persona, the skill spawns a general-purpose
subagent and tells it to read `agents/<file>.md` first. If a harness cannot
nest subagents, use direct dispatch instead of the synthesizer.

A Goldfish review needs a fresh context. If a harness has no subagent tool,
the review skills stop instead of running in the same context. Check actual
tool availability rather than inferring it from the product name. This applies
to standalone Antigravity IDE and to ChatGPT modes that do not expose native
fresh-context delegation.

Fresh conversation context does not mean that the host omits its instruction
files. Codex's `fork_context: false` and `fork_turns: "none"` isolate parent
turns; they do not establish that project or user instructions are excluded.
Keep stable workspace conventions in instruction files. State review
assumptions that the Goldfish must challenge as explicit review criteria.

## Artifact Directory

Skills write briefs, drafts, and reports to the working directory, or to the
harness's artifact directory if it has one. In Claude Code, Claude Cowork,
Codex, and ChatGPT, you can name another folder. Add this line to your prompt,
or to an agent instructions file that your harness loads (`CLAUDE.md` or
`AGENTS.md`, in the project or at user level):

```text
EGM artifact directory: .dev/docs
```

A relative path is relative to the working directory. If a path set in an
instructions file resolves outside the working directory, after following
symbolic links, EGM asks you to confirm it before creating the folder or
writing there. If you decline or no one can confirm, as in a headless run, the
files go to the working directory. The answer isn't saved, so a new session
asks again. A path in your prompt needs no confirmation. Design docs and other
project files do not move. Claude Code reads a project `AGENTS.md` only when
the project has no `CLAUDE.md`.

Commit approved specifications in `docs/designs/` and project rules in
`AGENTS.md`. Teammates and agents then use the same committed files. Add
`.dev/docs` to `.gitignore` only to keep scratch drafts out of git before
approval.

**Antigravity CLI**, **Claude Code**, and **Codex** pass automated installation

host-instruction leaks, not evidence that parent conversation turns leaked.

**Claude Cowork** ([#105](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/105)) and **ChatGPT Work** ([#106](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/106)) have working installation paths with open cloud trace verification gaps. End-to-end workflow fixtures passed on 2026-10-30 (brainstorm, draft, and uninterrupted review with 15 fresh-context reviewers); named `egm/egm-*` agents cannot be spawned in this runtime, so reviewers used the general-purpose fallback reading the installed persona first. Goldfish reviews stop if fresh-context, read-only subagent delegation is unavailable, and reviewers launch on the host's read-only subagent profile. Devin CLI 3000.12.43 runs on 2026-11-10 passed routing, human pauses, read-only reviewers, and parent-marker isolation with every file write denied, so no workflow ran to a final artifact. See the [harness test record](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/blob/main/TESTING.md#harness-test-record) for tested surfaces and limits.

### Contributing Support for New Harnesses

A harness counts as supported after `/egm-brainstorm`, `/egm-draft`, and
`/egm-review` run end to end through its plugin install. When contributing

Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.

Tradeoff: These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.

1. Think Before Coding

Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.

Before implementing:

State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.

If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.

If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.

If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.

2. Environment & Runtime

Ensure toolchain consistency before execution.

Always check for the presence of a .nvmrc file in the root directory.

Before installing dependencies, running scripts, or building the project, ensure the correct Node.js version is active in the current shell session:

export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"
nvm use


If nvm is not installed in the subshell, verify node -v matches .nvmrc before proceeding. If nvm use fails due to a missing local version, stop and log that nvm install is required.

3. Simplicity First

Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.

No features beyond what was asked.

No abstractions for single-use code.

No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.

No error handling for impossible scenarios.

If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.

Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.

4. Surgical Changes

Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.

When editing existing code:

Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.

Don't refactor things that aren't broken.

Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.

If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.

When your changes create orphans:

Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.

Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.

The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.

5. Goal-Driven Execution

Define success criteria. Loop until verified.

Transform tasks into verifiable goals:

"Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"

"Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"

"Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"

[Step] → verify: [check]

[Step] → verify: [check]

Strict Typing: Adhere to strict: true compiler rules. Explicitly type all variables, parameters, and return types where inference isn't structural or explicitly clear.

Functions & Methods: All exported functions, component props, and helper functions must include explicit parameter types and a return type annotation. Inline array callbacks (e.g., .map(), .filter()) may rely on contextual inference.

Specificity: Avoid using any. If a type is genuinely dynamic or unknown, use unknown and narrow it downstream using type guards or conditional blocks. Use is predicates for custom type guards.

# Suggested infrastructure for the Frame Inventory exercise.
#
# This compose file is a starting point, not a requirement. You are free to
# swap any of these services for tooling you prefer (a different database,
# search engine, message broker, hosting model, etc.) as long as the final
# stack still runs end-to-end with a single command.
#

services:
  backend:
    build:
      context: ./src/backend
    container_name: frame-inventory-backend
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE: docker
    depends_on:
      - postgres
      - opensearch
    networks:
      - frame-inventory

  frontend:
    build:
      context: ./src/frontend
    container_name: frame-inventory-frontend
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      BACKEND_URL: http://backend:8080
    volumes:
      - ./src/frontend/src:/app/src
      - ./src/frontend/public:/app/public
    depends_on:
      - backend
    networks:
      - frame-inventory

  postgres:
    image: postgres:18.6
    container_name: frame-inventory-postgres
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: frames

    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql
    networks:
